tasks.summary_en: How many solutions does $2\sin x+3\cos x=6$ have on $(0,2\pi)$?
tasks.statement_en: The equation $2\sin x+3\cos x=6$ on the interval $(0,2\pi)$: A. has no real solutions.  B. has exactly one real solution.  C. has exactly two real solutions.  D. has more than two real solutions.
tasks.notes: [audit: value carries no information] Max of 2 sin x + 3 cos x is sqrt(13) < 6, so no solutions exist.

tasks.statement_en: The first urn contains 3 white balls and 5 black balls, and the second urn contains 7 white balls and 2 black balls. One ball is drawn from the first urn, moved to the second urn, and two more balls of the same color as the drawn ball are added to the second urn. Then two balls are drawn from the second urn. Compute the probability of the event that both balls drawn from the second urn are white.

tasks.notes: Answer is two tangent-line equations (y=4x-7 and y=4x+67/27), not a single number.

tasks.statement_en: Given is the quadratic trinomial $f(x)=(m+1)x^2+2(m-2)x+m-4$. Determine all values of the parameter $m$ for which the trinomial $f$ has two distinct real roots $x_1$, $x_2$ satisfying the condition $x_1^2-x_2^2=x_1^4-x_2^4$.
tasks.notes: Unique valid m = (12+sqrt(109))/5; the other root of the auxiliary equation is outside the domain where f is a genuine quadratic with two distinct real roots.

tasks.notes: Task explicitly requires considering all possible cases: three distinct valid (a,b,c) triples exist ((-12,39,-28), (6,3,-10), (-3,-6,8)), so there is no single well-defined final numeric card value.

tasks.statement_en: Consider all cones whose axial cross-section is a triangle with perimeter 20. Compute the height and base radius of the cone among those considered whose volume is greatest. Compute that volume.
